item.title: Exploited SharePoint CVE-2026-32201 Chain, Malicious NuGet Packages, and AI Agent Access Risks
item.content:encoded:
CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, CVE-2026-56164: Frequently Asked Questions About Active Exploitation of Microsoft SharePoint Server Vulnerabilities — Must Read

CISA and Microsoft warn that multiple on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server flaws are being actively exploited to gain access, execute code, steal IIS machine keys and maintain persistence. Organizations should urgently apply Microsoft’s patches, enable AMSI/Defender detections, and review systems for compromise before rotating keys.

  • CISA confirmed active exploitation of three on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659 and CVE-2026-56164, and Microsoft later confirmed CVE-2026-58644 had also been exploited in the wild.
  • All five vulnerabilities covered in the alert affect all supported on-premises SharePoint Server versions: Subscription Edition, 2019 and 2016.
  • CISA said attackers have combined CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659 and CVE-2026-56164 to gain entry to SharePoint instances, extract IIS machine keys, establish persistence through deserialization techniques and deploy malware.
  • Microsoft released patches for all five vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, CVE-2026-56164, CVE-2026-55040 and CVE-2026-58644.
  • CISA and Microsoft published AMSI and Microsoft Defender Antivirus detection signatures for the three actively exploited vulnerabilities and recommended enabling AMSI integration with full request body scanning.

UK investigates TikTok for alleged age-verification lapses, exposing kids to online harms — May Read

UK regulator Ofcom is investigating TikTok over claims its age-check systems may have failed to identify many children, potentially exposing them to harmful content in violation of the Online Safety Act. TikTok denies wrongdoing and says it will work with Ofcom to show it meets its obligations.

  • Ofcom is investigating TikTok for allegedly failing to effectively verify users’ ages and inadequately protecting children online under the U.K.’s Online Safety Act.
  • Ofcom said TikTok’s age inference models may have failed to correctly identify a significant proportion of children, putting them at risk of exposure to harmful content.
  • Ofcom urged social media companies using age inference models for child protection duties to switch without delay to methods listed in its guidance as highly effective.
  • Companies that violate the Online Safety Act can be fined £18 million or 10% of qualifying worldwide revenue, and the British government can attempt to ban platforms in egregious cases.
  • TikTok said it strictly enforces age-appropriate experiences through platform rules and advanced age inference technologies, and that it is confident it meets its Online Safety Act obligations.

Ukrainians rally against dismissal of tech-minded defense minister Fedorov — May Read

Ukrainians protested President Zelensky’s unexplained dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who was seen as a key driver of drone adoption, digital military reform, and anti-corruption efforts. Reports suggest tensions with Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi may have contributed to the move.

  • Ukrainians protested across Kyiv, Lviv, Odesa and other cities after President Volodymyr Zelensky abruptly dismissed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
  • Fedorov was viewed by many younger Ukrainians and soldiers as a leading figure in efforts to modernize Ukraine’s military through drones and digital innovation while addressing corruption in the Defense Ministry.
  • Fedorov said his team disrupted Starlink satellite internet terminals used by Russian drone operators, supported strikes on Russian logistics in occupied Crimea, reformed military procurement, and bought more drones in four months than during the entire previous year.
  • Ukrainian media outlets cited anonymous government sources saying tensions between Fedorov and Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi contributed to the dismissal, and Fedorov confirmed he had advocated replacing Syrskyi.
  • Parliament approved Sergiy Koretsky as prime minister and most cabinet nominees, while defense and foreign minister candidates were expected to be submitted later.

Early Attack Warning Signals for AI and Agentic Security — Optional

Silent Push argues that AI-assisted security workflows are only useful if fed validated, early-warning intelligence, not stale IOCs from attacks already underway. Its Context Graph and MCP Server are positioned as a way to surface adversary infrastructure before campaigns launch and bring that data directly into existing SOC, IR, and CTI workflows.

  • Silent Push argues that AI-assisted security tools can produce fast but wrong conclusions when they are fed stale, unvalidated, or incomplete detection data.
  • The Silent Push Context Graph maps changes in DNS, WHOIS, certificate, and hosting data to surface Indicators of Future Attack before adversary infrastructure is weaponized.
  • The Silent Push MCP Server, released in version 6.0, lets practitioners query Context Graph intelligence in plain language inside Claude, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible platforms.
  • Silent Push says its Context Graph uses validated signals grounded in observed infrastructure behavior, includes clear data provenance, and is backed by more than 200 API endpoints.
  • Silent Push states that in May 2025 it identified staging domains behind what would become the Salt Typhoon campaign, with public reports of intrusions following two months later.

Finding Cleartext in Encrypted Gaming Traffic | Corelight — Optional

Corelight shows that ostensibly encrypted gaming traffic can still contain recoverable cleartext, creating visibility and data-leakage risks. The key takeaway is that defenders should inspect encrypted game-related network flows for plaintext artifacts rather than assuming encryption fully hides the contents.

  • The article is titled “Finding Cleartext in Encrypted Gaming Traffic | Corelight.”
  • The article focuses on finding cleartext in gaming traffic that is described as encrypted.
  • Corelight is identified in the article title as the source of the article.

AI Agents Broke the Security Playbook. Here's What Replaces It. — Optional

AI agents make enterprise environments too dynamic for fixed security workflows, because they can borrow credentials, access systems autonomously, and disappear quickly. The article argues security teams should use a live identity foundation to discover and govern agents, while building custom operational workflows on top.

  • AI agents can act autonomously, invoke tools, acquire access across systems, change behavior based on context, and sometimes borrow human access before disappearing ahead of inventory scans.
  • Token Security research found enterprise agent deployments ranging from human-triggered chatbots to autonomous production services, with more than a fifth of local agents already holding direct access to production data sources.
  • The article argues that fixed vendor security workflows cannot anticipate every organization-specific question about agent access, ownership, inherited credentials, and attack paths.
  • The article says security teams should buy foundational capabilities such as continuous discovery, integrations, normalization, identity correlation, access mapping, governance controls, auditability, and secure execution boundaries.
  • The article argues that security teams should build and own the operational layer of workflows, reports, reviews, and automations on top of a live identity foundation.

ThreatsDay: Game Cheat Spyware, 24-Hour Ransomware, Chrome Sync Stalking + 12 More Stories — Optional

This week’s threats show attackers turning trusted-looking tools, repos, installers, browser sync features, and exposed services into fast-moving compromise paths for spyware, infostealers, RATs, and ransomware. The key takeaway is to avoid granting trust by default: verify software sources, lock down accounts and exposed systems, patch known exploited flaws, and monitor small handoffs before they become full intrusions.

  • Researchers found 11 malicious NuGet packages posing as .NET game utilities, bots, and panels that download and run a second-stage Python payload called pepesoft.exe from GitHub Releases and Hugging Face paths under the username pepegit666.
  • Cisco Talos reported that the Russian-speaking, financially motivated actor UAT-11795 has used trojanized installers and ClickFix lures to deliver Starland RAT and a PowerShell-based C2 memory implant called WLDR agent to users in the U.S. and Europe.
  • Broadcom’s Symantec and Carbon Black Threat Hunter Team said a previously undocumented Rust-based ransomware family called Spirals was deployed across a South Asian IT services company’s network less than 24 hours after an initial breach through an internet-facing IIS web server.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-46817 in Oracle E-Business Suite and CVE-2023-4346 in KNX Association KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of active exploitation.
  • The article describes multiple fraud and malware campaigns, including more than 290 fake GitHub repositories distributing a BoryptGrab-lineage infostealer, Chrome Sync abuse for stalking, eCard-themed phishing pages delivering remote management tools, and a Vidar stealer plus XMRig miner campaign spread through malvertising.
